描述_EN: the image is nearly entirely gilded, apart from the hair, and was probably once covered by a thin layer of transparent lacquer. buddhism originated in india from the teachings of an indian prince, sakyamuni. he was probably born at the end of the 6th century bc in a small state in nepal, but decided to renounce his royal position to embark upon a monastic life. the bronze figure shows buddha in this precise moment: he is sitting in a meditative posture with his legs crossed, while his right hand extends downward to touch the soil in the symbolic gesture called 'bhumisparsamudra' (touching the earth). after resisting the attacks of mara, the goddess of evil, sakyamuni summoned up the earth goddess to bear witness to his achievement. after leaving his palace and and experiencing various spiritual revelations, he sat under a tree waiting for enlightenment, vowing not to move. this gilt bronze figure represents a crucial event in sakyamuni's life.
描述_ZN: 除头发外，图像几乎全部镀金，而且可能曾经被一层薄薄的透明漆覆盖。 佛教起源于印度，来自印度王子释迦牟尼的教义。 他可能于公元前6世纪末出生在尼泊尔的一个小国，但他决定放弃他的王室地位，开始了僧侣生活。 铜像显示了菩萨在这个精确的时刻：他以冥想的姿势盘腿而坐，而他的右手向下延伸，以象征性的姿态触摸土壤，称为 "bhumisparsamudra"（触摸大地）。 在抵抗了邪恶女神玛拉的攻击后，释迦牟尼召唤了大地女神来见证他的成就。 在离开他的宫殿并经历了各种精神启示之后，他坐在树下等待开悟，并发誓不再移动。 这个鎏金铜像代表了释迦牟尼生命中的一个重要事件。
